PullRequest.Title: Canvases: Avoid redundant Editor Canvas menu refreshes

## Summary

- compare Editor Window canvas definition lists structurally, matching the Agents Window registry
- avoid notifying menu observers when a refresh returns content-identical definitions
- verify that an unchanged refresh retains the existing Canvas submenu contribution

Follow-up to #341597 and #341498.

## Validation

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/canvases/browser/editorCanvasActions.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/canvases/test/browser/editorCanvasActions.test.ts` — passed
- `npm run test-browser-no-install -- --browser chromium --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/canvases/test/browser/editorCanvasActions.test.ts --reporter dot` — 2 passing
- pre-commit hygiene — passed

*🤖 Written by GitHub Copilot on behalf of @jruales.*

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Every canvas membership publication or subscription snapshot that returned content-identical definitions produced a fresh array, invalidated the observable, rescanned the full definitions/targets collections, and replaced the Canvas submenu registration, causing redundant MenuRegistry notifications and observer rebuilds.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Unchanged canvas refreshes caused avoidable menu refresh notifications and synchronous collection-wide menu reconciliation in the renderer.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The changed observable uses structuralEquals, so an unchanged flat definition catalog is rejected at set time. The catalog RPC still occurs, but collection-wide menu reconciliation, submenu disposal/recreation, MenuRegistry notifications, and dependent menu rebuilds are skipped unless catalog content changes.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The base observable used strict reference equality, while loadAvailableDefinitions always creates a fresh filtered/sorted array after listCanvases. Canvas definition notifications are emitted for ChatCanvasesChanged actions and snapshots, so an unchanged catalog still reran the definitions/targets autorun. That autorun scans all definitions and targets and always replaces submenuRegistration; MutableDisposable disposes the old MenuRegistry item and appends a new one, and both operations fire MenuRegistry change events that schedule menu refreshes. The added test explicitly fires an unchanged definition refresh and proves the submenu object is now retained.

Scenarios.Scenario: Populate the Editor Window Canvas submenu when an eligible Chat view/context becomes active
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The widget/context autorun schedules listCanvases; the submenu cannot show registered definitions until the browser-to-agent-host call, session/chat restoration, and two control-plane catalog RPCs complete. Filtering, sorting, observable comparison, and menu reconciliation then run synchronously in the renderer.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: listSessionCanvases crosses from the renderer-side local agent host service to the management/agent service and may restore/materialize the target session/chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical IPC listing per non-coalesced context/definitions refresh; bursts in the same delay window coalesce and in-flight bursts queue at most one follow-up.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical IPC listing and restoration path ran before the diff with the same scheduling and cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks initial registered-canvas menu population and each authoritative refresh result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The live Copilot session concurrently requests rpc.canvas.list and rpc.extensions.list to construct the definition catalog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two parallel control-plane RPCs per effective catalog listing, independent of C.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same two parallel RPCs were required before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both RPCs must complete before menu definitions can be filtered, sorted, and displayed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: C registered canvas definitions plus R reopenable canvas targets for the active chat. The new comparison examines the sorted flat C-entry catalog once; changed catalogs still reconcile O(C + R).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A zero-delay ThrottledDelayer coalesces same-tick triggers and a Throttler permits one list operation at a time with at most one accumulated follow-up. Inside one host list, canvas.list and extensions.list run in parallel.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no catalog-result cache: initial activation and each accepted definitions event invoke listing. A warm live session avoids cold restoration work; the new structural equality check acts only as a downstream unchanged-result dedupe and does not cache or suppress the remote list.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the call path, delayer serialization, RPC pair, flat definition shape, observable comparator, and menu autorun are directly established in code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact catalog size and cold session restoration latency vary, but the diff does not increase either boundary count. The new flat structural pass is bounded by catalog size and replaces larger downstream work for unchanged results.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Initial and changed-catalog paths add one small O(C) structural comparison, while all expensive boundary calls and concurrency remain unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Process a canvas membership/definition notification whose registered catalog is unchanged
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The notification schedules the same authoritative listing. After it returns, structuralEquals now stops propagation before the collection-wide definitions/targets autorun and MenuRegistry submenu replacement; this downstream work is off the remote request path but runs synchronously in the renderer after completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the authoritative canvas catalog after ChatCanvasesChanged actions, snapshots, or accepted snapshot refreshes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serialized listing per effective event after coalescing; at most one follow-up accumulates while a request is running.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same listing occurred, but its fresh array always invalidated availableDefinitions and triggered downstream menu work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the code can determine that the catalog is unchanged; the diff does not remove or delay this boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compare the previous and returned sorted arrays structurally in the renderer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One O(C) comparison per successful current listing; no retained copy and no work beyond the flat primitive catalog fields.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Strict reference equality accepted every newly allocated result array, so no content comparison occurred and downstream work always ran.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs immediately before observable notification; on equality it avoids O(C + R) menu reconciliation, submenu disposal/append, registry events, and dependent rebuilds.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: C definitions, R reopenable targets, and M live menu observers for ChatNewMenu/submenus. Comparison is O(C) over seven primitive fields per definition; before the diff every fresh array caused O(C + R) reconciliation and menu observer rebuild scheduling.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Same-tick events are coalesced; events arriving during one list produce at most one serialized follow-up. There is no concurrent burst of catalog requests.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The catalog is still fetched on each effective notification, including unchanged results. The current sorted result is retained as the positive downstream state; structural equality suppresses only content-identical observable updates. Failures preserve the prior state and are not negative-cached, unchanged by this PR.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: notification sources, fresh-array creation, observable equality semantics, unconditional submenu replacement, MenuRegistry event emission, and the retention test are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of live menu observers and event frequency depends on UI state and host activity, but the direction is unambiguously beneficial and the added comparison remains linear in a small flat catalog.
Scenarios.Verdict: Performance fix, not a finding. It removes redundant synchronous renderer/menu work while preserving remote refresh semantics.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a registered canvas command after an unchanged or changed catalog refresh
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command validates the currently available definition, optionally reveals an existing canvas, then invokes openSessionCanvas across the local agent-host boundary and the runtime canvas.open RPC. Structural deduplication occurs before command invocation and does not add work here.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: openSessionCanvas crosses to the agent host after validation, and the host invokes rpc.canvas.open.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one open RPC per explicit command execution; an existing live sourced canvas returns after reveal instead.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical validation, reveal, IPC, restoration, and runtime-open behavior existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks completion of the user-requested open action.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Validation scans C available definitions once per explicit user command; existing-canvas lookup scans the active chat canvases. Both were pre-existing.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One boundary operation per user command invocation; no new parallelism, limiter, or burst is introduced by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: An unchanged refresh retains the prior structurally identical definition objects and command registration. Changed content updates the catalog normally. No opening-result cache exists or is changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: command closure updates, validation, existing-canvas branch, and transitive open boundary are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Canvas counts and host RPC latency vary, but the diff neither changes command cardinality nor adds work to this path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; command behavior and expensive-boundary cost are unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and the performance pass. The production change replaces strict array identity with structural equality for a flat canvas-definition catalog. It fixes repeated renderer/menu work on unchanged authoritative refreshes, adds only a bounded linear comparison on successful listings, and does not change IPC/RPC cardinality, cache behavior, or concurrency. No performance findings were submitted; the verified regression fix was recorded against its introducing commit.
